title: Continuous deployment for AWS Lambda Web Functions with AWS CodePipeline
description: Release a Lambda Web Function from a Git commit with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild, creating an immutable revision and shifting the endpoint's revision weights to it.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: A Lambda Web Function is made of three resources. The function is the top-level resource, a revision is an immutable snapshot of code and configuration, and an endpoint has its own HTTPS domain and routes traffic to one or two revisions by weight. A single AWS::Serverless::WebFunction resource in the template expands into all three.

Web Functions accept code only as a reference to an object in a versioning-enabled Amazon S3 bucket, and there is no direct upload through the API. AWS SAM packages the code for the revision the stack creates, but releasing each commit needs the same glue in every team adopting Web Functions: produce a zip, put it in the bucket, create a revision that points at it, and move traffic to that revision.

On a push to the tracked branch, the AWS CodePipeline source action reads the commit through an AWS CodeConnections connection and writes it to the artifact bucket. AWS CodeBuild zips the source and calls s3api put-object. Because versioning is enabled, the response carries a VersionId. CodeBuild then calls lambda-web create-web-function-revision, passing the bucket, the key and that version. Pinning the revision to an object version is what makes the artifact immutable: a later upload to the same key cannot change what an existing revision runs. The revision records the commit SHA in the APP_COMMIT environment variable, so a response from the application identifies the commit it was built from.

CodeBuild waits for the revision to reach Active, then calls lambda-web update-web-function-endpoint with a single weight of 100 on it. That call is the release, not an optimisation. An endpoint's auto-deployment mode decides whether Lambda routes traffic to each new revision automatically, and AWS::Lambda::WebFunctionEndpoint has no auto-deployment property, so infrastructure as code cannot select LatestRevision. The AutoDeploymentMode property on the AWS SAM resource is used at transform time only, to pin the endpoint's weights to the revision the stack creates. A deployed endpoint is always in Disabled mode, which the documentation recommends for production, and a revision the pipeline creates becomes Active without receiving traffic until the weights move.

Rolling back is a routing change rather than a redeployment: put the weight on an earlier revision. Nothing is rebuilt, because revisions are immutable and their artifacts are still in the bucket. An endpoint routes to at most two revisions with weights totalling 100, which is the room a weighted canary works within.

Two behaviours are worth knowing. If a later stack update makes AWS CloudFormation create a new revision, CloudFormation also resets the endpoint's weights to it, so the pipeline's release stops serving traffic until the pipeline runs again. And 50 revisions per function is a cleanup target rather than a hard cap: Lambda deletes the oldest revisions that no endpoint routes to, which can include a rollback target removed from all weights.

The endpoint defaults to IamAuth, so unsigned requests are refused and callers need lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint. Setting EndpointAuthType to ApplicationManaged makes the endpoint public and leaves authorization to the application, which the sample application does not implement.
